title: OTLP ingest gateway: schema guard + Tempo prober
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an OTLP ingest gateway component that enforces incoming trace schema constraints (schema guard), normalizes legacy tag shapes, and runs a Tempo compatibility prober. The gateway should validate and either reject, sanitize, or tag malformed spans based on tenant policy; enrich traces that require Tempo-specific fields; and periodically probe Tempo endpoints with synthetic spans to detect API regressions or compatibility issues. The goal is to reduce noisy/failed exports to Tempo, provide clearer failure signals, and enable tenant-level sampling and fallback routing without increasing ingest latency beyond SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway validates required OTLP fields (trace_id, span_id, timestamp, name) and rejects invalid spans with 4xx and readable error codes
Malformed-but-recoverable spans are sanitized and annotated with a standard tag (redwood.trace.schema_fixup=true)
Tenant-configurable policy allows three behaviours: reject, sanitize+tag, forward-as-is
Tempo prober runs every 5 minutes per-region and reports probe histograms and last-success timestamp to observability dashboard
End-to-end tests covering legacy jaeger-encoded attributes -> normalized OTLP output
CPU and p99 latency overhead for ingest path remains <= 3ms added median and <= 10ms p99 on 95th percentile traffic mix compared to baseline
Feature rollout via canary on 5% of tenants with a quick rollback playbook
design_decisions: Do schema validation inline at gateway to provide immediate rejection feedback — trade-off: adds CPU but simplifies downstream exporters
Use a pluggable sanitizer pipeline: set of small deterministic transforms (timestamp coercion, tag name normalization, traceid padding) so we can enable/disable per-tenant
Prober will use a lightweight synthetic span generator and send via existing Tempo write API (not instrumented services) to isolate exporter compatibility checks
Sampling decisions are tenant-scoped and resolved from remote config (feature flag service); defaults fall back to global sampling settings
Buffering for transient Tempo outages uses a small in-memory ring + write-behind to Kafka for durable replay — configurable per-tier
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete — validated that header-level schema checks can be implemented with sub-millisecond overhead using protobuf fast path (PR: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/487).
2026-02-28: Prototype sanitizer built; supports timestamp coercion and attribute key normalization. Early benchmark shows +1.2ms median, +6ms p99 on small instances.
2026-03-03: UX/PM review — agreed to surface 'schema_fixup' tag in trace metadata and add an alert when >0.5% of tenant spans are sanitized in a 5m window.
2026-03-06: Security review requested — gateway will accept encrypted OTLP/gRPC; KMS keys for prober credentials proposed. (security_review_required=true)
2026-03-09: Integration test harness for Tempo prober running; discovered Tempo rejects spans missing process.serviceName — added enrichment step in sanitizer.
2026-03-12: Ready for internal canary rollout config. Working on playbook and dashboard panels for probe health and sanitizer rate by tenant.
notes: Rollout plan: feature flag gated; 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if sanitizer rate > 2% or p99 ingest latency degrades > 15%
Monitoring: add metrics otlp.gateway.sanitized_spans_total, otlp.gateway.rejected_spans_total, tempo.prober.latency_ms, tempo.prober.last_success_timestamp
Runbook snippet: If tempo prober fails regionally for >15 minutes, switch fallback to kafka+replay mode and notify SRE on-call
Open question: whether to persist sanitized original payload (for debugging) — currently plan to drop full payload for PII concerns and keep a short checksum + tag
